comparison.objective: Fit color-matched caps to four pens and sort the completed pens into marked areas; the candidate sets, locks, and functionally verifies an industrial gripper opening stop.
comparison.physical_skill: PR-360 tests color matching, repeated coaxial cap insertion, bimanual part handling, release, and sorting. It lacks screw adjustment, wrench/driver countertorque, setpoint preservation during locknut tightening, and articulated retention testing.
comparison.success_condition: PR-360 gives per-pen credit for a matching cap retained after insertion and hands-clear dwell, plus placement credit when the released capped pen rests inside its color area; full score requires all four capped and sorted. The candidate instead requires specified opening accuracy, installed nuts, three repeat cycles, bounded drift, and released clearance. Available versions disclose that simulated cap retention uses a pose-preserving joint and that physical force qualification is unverified; otherwise the scoring rubric is complete.
comparison.reason: Generic insertion, bimanual handling, and release are insufficient for overlap: PR-360 measures repeated closure assembly and color sorting, not torque-coupled adjustment locking or preservation of a mechanical setting through functional cycles.
